To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) a new method for determining the ultimate capacity of beam-to-column welded connections is presented, (b) a fracture mechanics approach to evaluate the fracture toughness demands of welded connections is proposed, (c) a finite element method for simulating the fracture behavior of welded connections is developed, and (d) the fracture mechanics based method is applied to evaluate the fracture resistance of welded beam-to-column connections.
the fracture mechanics analyses of welded beam-to-column connections can be performed by using two-dimensional finite element models.
The fracture toughness demands of welded beam-to-column connections with various design details are quantified by the fracture mechanics based finite element analyses.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the seismic behavior of welded beam-to-column connections, which are the most commonly used connections for steel moment resisting frames in China.
the fracture behavior and fracture toughness demands for welded beam-to-column connections of steel moment resisting frame structures.
the seismic performance evaluation of welded beam-to-column connections.

the present research has provided a significant contribution to the field of fracture mechanics and to the understanding of the fracture behavior of beam-to-column steel connections.
the results of this study are very encouraging.

the beam-to-column connection fracture mechanics is a useful tool to evaluate the fracture resistance of the connections and the fracture toughness demand of the welded joint.
the fracture mechanics approach is an effective tool for the fracture resistant analysis and design of steel beam-to-column connections.
the fracture toughness of the beam-to-column connections can be improved by removing the weld backing bar and reinforcing the fillet welds.

the weld HAZ in the beam flange is a critical area where the fracture is likely to initiate.
